shortDescription: President Trump said Wednesday that the Iran war likely will not end until "right after" the November 3 midterm elections, and that significant relief from elevated gasoline prices would not come before then, indicating little prospect of a near-term de-escalation in the seven-month-long conflict."…

children: President Trump said Wednesday that the Iran war likely will not end until "right after" the November 3 midterm elections, and that significant relief from elevated gasoline prices would not come before then, indicating little prospect of a near-term de-escalation in the seven-month-long conflict.
"Right after the election, oil prices are going to be tumbling downward," Trump told reporters. "It's going to take a little bit longer than the midterms."

Trump, who has routinely predicted that the Middle East conflict would wrap up quickly following an Iranian collapse, described a new narrative Wednesday that Iran's strategy now is to hang on through the U.S. election.

Iran is "desperate to try and affect the election so that we can get a nice, weak group of people [in Congress] and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon," Trump said, but "the war will end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer."
The president also said record-breaking prices at the pump will fall below $2/gal, "but not until after the midterms."

The U.S.-Iran standoff has escalated in recent days, with U.S. forces destroying eight Iranian tankers in the Persian Gulf area since September 5 in response to attempted Iranian missile attacks on U.S. warships; "You're going to see a lot more" attacks on Iranian tankers, Trump said.

The national average price for gasoline reached $4.22/gal on Wednesday, according to AAA, up ~$0.07 from Tuesday and well over $1.00 from a year ago, and the U.S. average diesel price hit $5.94/gal, up ~$0.04 from the previous day and nearly $2.25 higher than last year at this time.

Meanwhile, U.S. diesel inventories are projected to fall this month to their lowest level in more than 20 years, according to the latest Short-Term Energy Outlook published by the Energy Information Administration.
The EIA also hiked its retail diesel price forecast for Q4 2026 by 14% to $5.55/gal and raised its wholesale price forecast by 33% from a month earlier.
"Diesel history is about to be made," GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan wrote on a social media post. "$6/gal nationally, never seen before, days away, it's now in the pipeline, unavoidable."
The big three U.S. refining companies—Marathon Petroleum
, Valero Energy
, and Phillips 66
—all posted all-time highs on Wednesday.
In regular trading, Brent crude futures
and U.S. crude topped $96/bbl, while front-month Nymex October ULSD (
) surged 5.1% $4.801/gal—its second-highest close in history—amid the escalating hostilities between the U.S. and Iran.
Front-month Nymex crude
for October delivery jumped 3.2% to $96.05/bbl, and front-month Brent crude
for November delivery rallied 3.3% to $101.21/bbl, the highest settlement values for both benchmarks since May 22; front-month Nymex October RBOB gasoline (
), however, fell 1.3% to $3.2106/gal, snapping a three-session winning streak.

U.S. natural gas futures fell as the market looked beyond this week’s inventory report to cooler weather that likely will cut demand; the front-month Nymex October contract slipped 3.2% to $2.822/MMBtu.

title: Trump says motorists likely will not see lower gas prices until after midterm elections
